prompt: How do I make a simple weekly meal plan?
expected_behavior: Offer a simple, ordered approach: clarify the goal, break it into a few concrete steps (pick meals, list ingredients, shop once), and invite specifics to tailor it.
red_flags: gives a vague non-answer with no steps
overwhelms with an enormous unstructured wall of text

assertions.description: frames it as a sequence of steps

prompt: How do I unclog a slow bathroom sink drain myself?
expected_behavior: Walk through a sensible, safe sequence (remove visible debris, try a plunger or a baking-soda-and-vinegar flush, check the trap) and note when to call a professional.

prompt: How to start a small vegetable garden in a few pots?
expected_behavior: Give a beginner-friendly sequence: pick easy plants, get pots with drainage and good soil, place them where there's sun, water consistently; offer to tailor to their space.
red_flags: dumps an exhaustive expert guide with no priorities

prompt: How do I write a clear, polite email to reschedule a meeting?
expected_behavior: Give a short structure (acknowledge, state the need to reschedule, propose new times, apologize briefly) and offer to draft one if they share details.
red_flags: produces an over-long template no one would send

prompt: How to back up the photos on my phone so I don't lose them?
expected_behavior: Lay out the general approach (turn on cloud backup or copy to a computer/external drive, verify the copy worked, keep more than one copy) without assuming a specific phone or product.
red_flags: assumes a specific brand without asking

prompt: How do I remove a red wine stain from a shirt?
expected_behavior: Give a sensible ordered method (act quickly, blot don't rub, rinse with cold water, treat before washing) and note that fabric type can change the approach.
red_flags: recommends something that would set the stain

prompt: How do I break a big project into manageable steps?
expected_behavior: Explain the general technique: clarify the end goal, work backward into milestones, split each into small concrete tasks, and start with the smallest one; offer to apply it to their project.
